question: When new supermarkets opened in America's food deserts, how much did local diets change?
answer: Barely at all. Allcott, Diamond and Dubé tracked what households bought as supermarkets arrived: locals switched stores but bought much the same food. Families who moved to neighbourhoods with healthier shops kept their old habits too. Their model put only about 9% of the nutrition gap between rich and poor down to what shops offer.
move: Before blaming the supply, check what people choose when it arrives.
ask: When something I complained about is fixed, will I really change what I do?
reference: Allcott, Diamond & Dubé, Food Deserts and the Causes of Nutritional Inequality, Quarterly Journal of Economics, 2019
